name: Offer of 30% off when the cap is 20% (real)

content.text: 🔥 Big news! This week only, enjoy 30% off all Grills at Ember & Spice Grill – from our famous Mixed Grill Platter to Lamb Chops and Seekh Kebabs. Come hungry, leave happy 😋 See you soon!

sources.data: Warm, friendly and family-run. We talk to customers like regulars, even on their first visit. Short, upbeat sentences with a little East London charm. Use the customer's first name. One or two emojis at most (🔥 😋 🙏), never a wall of them. Never pushy or salesy. Always say thank you. On bad reviews: apologise sincerely, never argue, and invite them back to make it right.
Please ask our staff about allergens before you order.

recent: Lamb Chops (4 pcs) are down to £11.15 this week 🔥 And remember, we're open till midnight every Friday for your late-night cravings. See you soon at Ember & Spice Grill!

checks.reason: Profile tone says never pushy or salesy and to use the customer's first name. 'Big news!' and 'Come hungry, leave happy' feel salesy, and there is no thank you or first name.
checks.fix: Rewrite in a warm, regulars-style voice with a thank you, and no hype opener.

checks.reason: Copy is generic ('Come hungry, leave happy', 'See you soon') and has no specific detail such as the address, charcoal grilling or opening hours.
checks.fix: Add something specific to Ember & Spice, such as the charcoal grill or the Whitechapel Road location.

checks.reason: Closing 'See you soon' repeats the closing of the previous output ('See you soon at Ember & Spice Grill!'). Opening 🔥 also repeats the emoji use.
checks.fix: Use a different closing line and opening.

checks.reason: Contains an en-dash used as a dash ('Grill – from our famous'), which is the same kind of dash the style rules ban. The two emojis (🔥 😋) are allowed by the profile, and there are no banned words. The dash needs fixing, and a minor fix is listed.
checks.fix: Replace the en-dash with a comma, as listed in minor_fixes.

checks.reason: 'our famous Mixed Grill Platter' is not supported by any source. 'This week only' is not in the owner's request, which gave no dates.
checks.fix: Remove 'famous' and 'This week only', or get real dates from the owner.

checks.reason: 30% off does not match the discount cap source of 20%.
checks.fix: Use a discount at or under 20%, or ask the owner to approve a change to the cap.

checks.reason: 'This week only' gives no start or end date. Dates must be explicit and consistent.
checks.fix: State exact dates, for example 'from Saturday 10 October to Friday 16 October', once the owner confirms them.

checks.reason: 'Lamb Chops' and 'Seekh Kebabs' do not match the menu names 'Lamb Chops (4 pcs)' and 'Seekh Kebab (2 pcs)'. 'Seekh Kebabs' is a plural form of the name.
checks.fix: Use 'Lamb Chops' and 'Seekh Kebab' exactly as on the menu.

checks.reason: Offer terms are unclear: no dates, no conditions (dine-in or takeaway, whether it covers every Grills item), and 'all Grills' is vague. 'This week only' creates urgency without a stated end.
checks.fix: State the discount, exact dates, and where it applies.

checks.reason: Maker rules broken: 30% is over the 20% cap, so needs_owner_input should have been set and no draft written. Offer dates and conditions are missing. The channel is whatsapp, which is blocked for now (email only).
checks.fix: Do not draft. Set needs_owner_input explaining the cap is 20% and ask how to proceed. Use the email channel.

recorded.notes: The main problem is the 30% discount, which is over the 20% cap. The maker should have set needs_owner_input and not drafted. Send back to the maker to ask the owner whether to run 20% instead, and to confirm the dates.
